Approve the policy vocabulary for branch-conditioned taint sanitizers (bifrost-dev #7578; shared by Java and Go parity)? It extends the existing `(sanitizer ...)` entry and its catalog JSON form; it adds no new entry kind. A conditional sanitizer uses `:when`, `:sanitizes` and optional `:requires` in place of `:input` and `:output`; the validator enforces one shape or the other. The trace was inconclusive. It found four possible exits where the sink could be dropped (`taint_policy.rs:6038`, `:6150`, `:6296` and `:15017`), but no product surface shows which one line 57 takes. I'll read the report's description of those exits, then decide between instrumenting them and bisecting.

The selector itself is where the site is lost. In the policy run, the `File.exists` sink selector selects **0** rows. The same selector, run as a direct query, returns line 57. One-argument calls such as `setReadable(true)` select 1 row each and become bound endpoints.

So the loss is inside the policy's compiled selector, before sink admission. The trace flagged one candidate: `selector_compiler.rs` drops receiver-only call-binding rows. I'll read that code myself; it is a short, specific read.
I'll make the experimental edit in the scratch worktree. It won't be committed; the real fix goes on its own branch after the experiment confirms it.
While the experiment runs, I'll read the routed guidance the real fix will need. That is the cache-identity rules for a policy change that alters retained findings, and the RQL and policy guidance.
The filter came from b1b77f63a0, "Fix retained taint findings under incomplete selector discovery (#3732)". I'll look at which tests that commit added.

The #3712 fixture shape fits: a Java source with a modeled sink, a `Gap.java` that makes discovery incomplete, and a `require-model` taint policy. A new case `policy-selector-incompleteness/receiver-only-sink` can follow it. It would have a zero-argument receiver sink, a one-argument control, and the gap file, so the test fails without the fix.

I'll wait for the experiment before filing the issue or starting the branch. If accepting receiver rows doesn't restore the 13 sites, the diagnosis is wrong.

Confirmed. With exact receiver rows accepted, the native route goes from 40 TP and 19 misses to **53 TP and 6 misses**. All 13 zero-argument receiver sinks change from miss to TP. There are no new extras and no sites lost, and the default route is unchanged. That is better than 0.15.0's native figure of 51.

I'll file the issue and fix it on its own branch from master.
#10014 is filed, labelled and assigned. Now the branch: a lane from current master, with the code change and the epoch token done by me. A child then writes the golden case and runs the validation.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- This regression came from an interaction, not from a changed line. The per-row filter from #3732 already rejected receiver-only rows. It only mattered once discovery was incomplete, and in this corpus unrelated stub files make every selector incomplete. That is why reading the history of the filter found nothing.
- The "individually usable row" rule exists so that one bad row doesn't erase every proven row (#3732, #5245). The fix keeps that rule. A receiver row must still carry the same site proof as a positional row; the only thing that changes is that receiver identity counts in place of argument identity.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

I found and fixed the cause of the native path-injection regression, tracked as **#10014**. When selector discovery is incomplete, the policy keeps only rows that identify their operand on their own, and an exact receiver row didn't count. A zero-argument call has only that receiver row, so sinks like `((File) source()).exists()` selected nothing. In the CodeQL CWE-022 test, unrelated stub files make discovery incomplete for every selector.

- **Experiment:** I rebuilt the native binary with the fix and reran packs#145's gate. It went from 40 TP / 0 extras / 19 misses to **53 TP / 0 extras / 6 misses**: exactly the 13 zero-argument receiver sinks were recovered. No site was lost, and the default route is unchanged.
- **Branch:** `10014-receiver-taint-rows` (commit 5f4f89c73e). It has the fix in `usable_taint_row` and the policy epoch token `-10014-receiver-taint-rows`.
- **Running:**

  - Child 308e8847 is checking whether the 6 remaining native misses are David's #10000, overloaded JDK constructors resolving as exhaustive with zero targets. The misses include `new File("")`, `new BufferedReader(...)` and `Files.write` with an Iterable.
